text:
Maya Singh: Quick idea: add a tiny feature to let an admin temporarily top up an API key from the org pool to handle short spikes (deploys, retries). call it "quota handoff" or "key top-up".
Ben Park: +1 but we need strict rules so it can't be used to bleed the org pool. logging and audit first.
Carmen Ruiz: telemetry ask: any request that uses transferred credits must set a span tag so we can filter traces by origin. also expose a metric for handoff consumption.
RateLimitBot: [auto] new proposal object created: quota_handoff_draft {grant_id, amount, ttl_secs, granted_by, reason} 
Maya Singh: enforcement model I sketched: treat handoff as a short-lived lease object. runtime flow: try key bucket -> key handoff bucket -> org bucket fallback. grant atomically moves credits from org free pool to key handoff bucket.
Darren O'Neill: technical: implement as a Redis atomic transfer (Lua) that creates a TTL key for the grant and adjusts counters. need idempotent grant API (grant_id) so retries don't double-transfer.
Alice Chen: UI: grant modal in console with amount, TTL, reason, and approver. once granted show a banner on the key page listing active grants and expiry timers. toast: "Granted 3,000 tokens to svc-payments (30m)"
Ben Park: policy knobs: per-grant absolute cap (100k tokens by default) + pct-of-org cap (e.g., max 20% of current free pool). also a per-key handoff consumption rate so it can't be drained instantly by retries.
Maya Singh: CLI example: 
```
rictl quota topup grant --org redwood-inc --key svc-payments-9 --amount 3000 --ttl 30m --reason "deploy window" --actor maya
```
Carmen Ruiz: tracing conventions: set attributes quota.handoff.used=true ; quota.handoff.id=<grant_id> ; quota.handoff.granted_by=<user>. add logs that mark each token withdrawal as "handed-off" vs "org".
Darren O'Neill: approval workflow suggestion: small grants (<=5k) auto-approve; medium (5k-50k) auto if org_pool above threshold; >50k manual approver. internal services can call API to request grants; UI shows pending approvals.
Ben Park: runtime fallback behavior: if handoff empty, fall back to normal key allowance. if org pool insufficient at grant time, grant fails with clear error and suggested alternatives.
Maya Singh: concurrency concerns: two grants racing must be guarded by the same LUA script to avoid double counts. also support revoke and extension by grantor. revoke should atomically return unused credits to org pool.
Alice Chen: UX edge cases: overlapping grants to same key -> show aggregated remaining handoff plus per-grant rows. if a grant is extended, update the countdown and audit entry. show who revoked/extended.
Carmen Ruiz: metrics: gauge for org_free_pool, gauge for handoff_grants_active, counter quota_handoff_consumed_total{key,org}. dashboard panel with handoff usage heatmap. alert when org_free_pool < 10%.
Ben Park: tests: concurrent grant attempts, TTL expiry reconsumption to org pool, partial grant when org pool smaller than requested, consumption rate enforcement.
Darren O'Neill: rollout plan: feature-flagged behind ent tier; land runtime primitives + rictl + minimal console; enable for one internal service for 2 weeks; iterate.
Maya Singh: RBAC: only org admins and role quota_granter can grant; we should support delegated service owners. every action must write an audit log entry (who, what, reason).
Ben Park: billing: tag usage rows with origin so billing exports can show billable vs org-credited usage. even if org pays, we want attribution.
RateLimitBot: [auto] RFC opened: https://go/repo/rfcs/362 (quota_handoff_proposal)
Maya Singh: next step: I'll draft RFC with JSON schema for grant object + pseudo-code for Lua transfer. tagging @eng-platform for review.
Carmen Ruiz: I'll own dashboard and tracing spec.
Darren O'Neill: I'll own runtime + LUA + tests. Ben + Maya will take CLI + console.
Maya Singh: default TTL suggestion = 30m, allow extensions up to 24h with manual approval. closing thread for now :wave:
